baseline_model: finetuned_detector_blend70.pt (70% v4 + 30% v3 weight blend, made by training/combine_models.py)
notes: Re-baselined on purpose when the production model changed from v3 (confidence 0.7) to the 70% v4 / 30% v3 blend (confidence 0.8). The blend trades a little hand-labelled close-up recall (24/33 vs 27/33 on this benchmark) for far fewer false alarms (28/300 vs 50/300) and fewer people false alarms (4/60 vs 6/60). Same tolerance rule as version 1: limits allow one more missed hand label, three more missed iNaturalist photos, three more false-alarm photos and one more people false-alarm photo than the baseline; larger regressions fail. Same fixed benchmark photos.

history.notes: Fixed subset selected by SHA256(sbb-accuracy-v1: + relative path) before scoring: 32 Open Images val hand-labelled photos (33 boxes), 150 supplied held-out iNaturalist test photos, and 60 val negatives in each of people/birds/lights/animals/other. Exclusive group precedence: people, birds, lights, animals, other. iNaturalist is held-out test, not Open Images val. Limits allow exactly one additional missed hand label, three additional missed iNaturalist photos, three additional overall false-alarm photos, and one additional people false-alarm photo relative to byte-identical v3 production at confidence 0.7. Larger regressions fail. These are regression tolerances, not confidence bounds or deployment safety requirements. Hand recall uses one-to-one IoU >= 0.3; iNaturalist uses any detection; alarms count photos. Default config confidence is the baseline; confidence overrides are scored as configured against the same fixed limits. Run slow GPU gate explicitly; set SBB_SKIP_ACCURACY=1 for fast suite.
